standard.title: How People Observe and Question
standard.description: explore the ways people make and use observations and questions to learn about the natural world
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior science learning assumed.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore how people — including scientists, First Nations Australians and themselves — use their senses and tools to make observations, and use questions to guide their learning about the natural world.

nodes.label: People use observations and questions to learn about the natural world
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe at least two ways people make observations and explain that scientists (and others) ask questions about what they observe.
nodes.minimum_width: Students describe two ways people make observations and give one example of a question a scientist or person might ask.
nodes.typical_width: Students use senses to make observations; explore how scientists use both senses and equipment; view examples of observations (rock paintings, photographs, drawings, reports); engage with stories about scientists like Jane Goodall or Joseph Banks; and notice how they make observations and ask questions.
wider: Explore how First Nations Australians gain knowledge about the land and its resources through observation — examining observation as a knowledge-building practice
Interact with stories or documentaries about scientists and notice the ways they make and record observations
Watch an age-appropriate documentary and notice how scientists, engineers and citizen scientists ask questions — then pose their own questions

response_modes.reason: First Nations land observation knowledge and documentary-style scientist stories provide culturally rich and varied contexts for the concept that observation and questioning are universal knowledge-building practices — not just school science activities.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations land observation knowledge and documentary scientist stories provide culturally rich and engaging directions grounded in elaborations.
success_criteria: Describes at least two ways people make observations (using senses and/or tools)
Gives one example of a question a scientist or person might ask about nature
